claim.statement: On 24 April 2026 Iran arrested a niece of the Khamenei family after she publicly condemned the regime — a rare visible-fissure inside the Supreme Leader's own family during the post-war legitimacy crisis.
claim.subject: Iranian security forces

assessment.uncertainty: Single second-tier outlet; specific niece's identity and exact charge not clear from headline.

claim.statement: On 18 April 2026, Dominica revoked the Citizenship-by-Investment status of a second Shamkhani brother — a son or relative of Ali Shamkhani (former Supreme National Security Council secretary) — over concealed Iranian ties; the Caribbean exit hatch the regime's elite uses for hedging is publicly closing.
claim.subject: Government of Dominica

claim.statement: By 21 April 2026 multiple opposition outlets were openly cataloguing the offshore wealth and lifestyles of Iranian regime officials' children (aghazadeh) — Sasha Sobhani's Ibiza jets, the Shamkhani Caribbean passports — sharpening the public salience of elite-vs-people inequality during the rial collapse.
claim.subject: Aghazadeh visibility

evidence.summary: Iran Focus piece on smuggled-wealth management.

claim.statement: By 28 April 2026 a global movement was openly rallying to save Iranian rapper Toomaj Salehi from execution — the case becoming the headline test of whether the post-war regime executes its highest-profile artist-prisoners.
claim.subject: International solidarity movement

claim.statement: On 27 April 2026, per HRANA, Iran's Supreme Court confirmed the death sentence of Mohammad Abbasi and a 25-year prison sentence for Fatemeh Abbasi — extending the post-ceasefire pattern of accelerated execution affirmations.
claim.subject: Iran Supreme Court

claim.statement: By late April 2026 Lebanese and Arab outlets (Lebanon24, Elsiyasa) were openly reporting that Iran's worsening financial crisis was forcing Tehran to scale back support for Hezbollah and possibly reduce the Lebanese militia's role inside Iran's strategic-depth architecture — a structural retreat from the proxy model.
claim.subject: Iran

evidence.summary: Elsiyasa: Iran financial crisis worsens, no Hezbollah support.

assessment.uncertainty: Direction confirmed by multiple Arab outlets; magnitude and timeline of reduction not quantified.

claim.statement: On 22 April 2026 Bloomberg published that Xi Jinping's support for Iran has explicit limits — corroborated by RFE/RL on 17 April warning that hopes China can push Iran toward peace are misplaced — shrinking the external-rescue scenario for Tehran.
claim.subject: Xi Jinping / China

claim.statement: On 30 April – 1 May 2026, organised protests in Vancouver and elsewhere demanded that FIFA ban Iran from the 2026 World Cup, with the message 'they are not representing Iran' — an explicit attempt to delegitimise the regime through sport while the football federation simultaneously filed an official protest about the Qatar-match referee.
claim.subject: Iranian-diaspora protesters
claim.object: FIFA ban Iran from 2026 World Cup

claim.statement: On 29 April 2026 Persian outlets characterised currency and gold prices in Iran as undergoing an 'explosive surge', consistent with mass conversion of rials into hard stores of value as the cease-fire-driven currency-market reopen accelerated capital flight.
claim.subject: IRR vs gold/USD

claim.statement: By 21 April 2026 the US Treasury had reportedly stepped up tracking of billions of dollars in capital flight leaving Iran, exposing a parallel hard-currency drain on top of the visible rial collapse.
claim.subject: Iran capital

assessment.uncertainty: Single low-tier source; specific volume figures not corroborated by Treasury OFAC press releases as of capture date.

claim.statement: On 27 April 2026 a regime-aligned outlet stated that 50 Iranian hospitals had been damaged during the war and 40,000 patients had received free treatment — a regime-side casualty tally implying significant strategic-target overlap with healthcare infrastructure.
claim.subject: Iranian hospitals

assessment.uncertainty: Regime-aligned source; figures cannot be independently verified during internet blackout.

claim.statement: On 23 April 2026, Médecins Sans Frontières publicly assessed that access to essential medical care in Iran remained fragile despite the ceasefire — corroborating the regime-side hospital-damage tally and the prior drug-price/morphine warnings.
claim.subject: MSF

claim.statement: As of 17 and 25 April 2026, Persian press (TABNAK, Eghtesad Journal) reported that the customary release of Zayandeh-Rud water for Isfahan farmers — a politically loaded annual decision — was being pushed to late Ordibehesht (mid-May), reopening the Isfahan farmer-water-rights flashpoint at the height of the post-war crisis.
claim.subject: Zayandeh-Rud release schedule

evidence.summary: Eghtesad Journal: probable late Ordibehesht reopening.

operations.rationale: Internal-family arrest amid external-proxy retreat illustrates the regime simultaneously losing legitimacy at the apex and abandoning frontier commitments.
Loss of Shamkhani Caribbean passport is the most concrete expression of the broader aghazadeh-visibility trend.
With Chinese backing capped, Iran has fewer external resources to underwrite Hezbollah; both sit on the regime's external-rescue collapse.
MSF independent assessment corroborates regime-side hospital-damage scale.
Gold/currency surge and tracked capital flight describe two faces of the same flight-to-safety dynamic.

synthesis.title: Cracks at depth, 17 Apr – 1 May 2026 — apex, axis, alloy
synthesis.summary: Three deeper-cut fissures complete the picture. APEX (the Khamenei family + aghazadeh): a Khamenei niece was arrested on 24 Apr after publicly condemning the regime, while Dominica revoked the Caribbean citizenship of a second Shamkhani-family member on 18 Apr — closing the elite hedging hatch and signalling a visible split inside the apex itself. AXIS (the proxy and external-backer architecture): Lebanese press (Lebanon24, Elsiyasa) on 29 Apr reported that Iran is reducing its support for Hezbollah, while Bloomberg (22 Apr) and RFE/RL (17 Apr) document that Xi Jinping's support has explicit limits — Iran's strategic-depth and external-rescue scenarios are simultaneously cratering. ALLOY (legitimacy in the cultural surface): an organised diaspora movement on 30 Apr–1 May demanded that FIFA ban Iran from the 2026 World Cup ('they are not representing Iran'); a global movement campaigned to halt Toomaj Salehi's execution; the Supreme Court confirmed the Abbasi family death sentences on 27 Apr; healthcare is fragile per MSF on top of 50 reported damaged hospitals; and gold/currency are in 'explosive surge' alongside US-tracked capital flight. The Zayandeh-Rud release is being pushed to late Ordibehesht — re-arming the Isfahan-farmer flashpoint at the worst possible moment. Read together with the prior 19 cracks in iran-cracks/ and iran-margins/, the regime's apex, axis, and alloy are degrading in lockstep — i.e., the failure modes are no longer single-domain.
synthesis.limitations: The Khamenei-niece arrest rests on a single second-tier wire; verify before high-confidence use. Lebanon24/Elsiyasa Hezbollah pieces are directionally clear but qualitatively-framed; magnitude unproven. JaFaJ capital-flight claim is low-tier and should be re-anchored to a Treasury OFAC release before promotion above 'medium' confidence.
